steps.a: Found the cause. The plain HTTP seat-map route creates a SeatMapSubscription and registers its onChange on the shared seatEvents emitter for every request, then returns a one-off JSON snapshot without ever calling off(). Only the WebSocket path removes its listener. Each request leaks a listener entry, a closure and a subscription object (heap grew ~460 MB over a 10-minute load test, dominated by those three types). The leak was masked because setMaxListeners(0) disables Node's MaxListenersExceeded warning. The likely fix is not to subscribe at all on the HTTP route (it only needs the snapshot), and to restore a listener limit so this shows up again; I haven't changed any code yet.

reference.summary: Diagnosed a Node.js memory leak causing out-of-memory kills: heap snapshot diffs under load showed listener entries, closures and subscription objects growing, traced to an HTTP route that adds an event emitter listener per request and never removes it, hidden because the max-listeners warning had been disabled. No fix was applied; removing the subscription from the route and restoring the listener limit was proposed.
facts: Production pods were OOM killed roughly every six hours
A 10-minute load test on staging grew the heap from about 148 MB to 611 MB
Heap diff growth was dominated by closures, listener entries and subscription objects
The HTTP seat-map route registers a listener per request without removing it; only the WebSocket path removes it
